# Report support SLA breaches

The support desk runs its tickets in the `tickets` service, which you can use through the `tickets` MCP server.

The support SLA policy is kept in the open ticket labeled `sla-policy`. Apply it to every ticket it covers, measured up to now, 2026-09-14 09:00 UTC, and find the tickets that breached their first-response target, their resolution target, or both.

1. Add exactly one comment to each breached ticket, with the text `SLA breach: <metrics>`, where `<metrics>` is `first-response`, `resolution`, or `first-response, resolution`. A ticket that already has a comment starting with `SLA breach:` was reported by an earlier review: do not comment on it again.
2. Create one ticket that reports the review:
   - title: `SLA breach report 2026-09-14`
   - team: `support-ops`
   - priority: `P2`
   - labels: `sla-report`
   - body: one line per breached ticket, including those reported by an earlier review, in ascending id order, in the form `#<id> <metrics>`, and nothing else

Do not change the status or priority of any ticket, and do not change, comment on or create any other ticket.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.
I'll start by discovering the tickets MCP tools.

Holidays without business hours: 2026-09-07.\\nOnly business time counts toward a target.\\n\\nTargets in business hours:\\n- P1: first response 1h, resolution 8h\\n- P2: first response 4h, resolution 16h\\n- P3: first response 8h, resolution 40h\\n- P4: first response 16h, resolution 80h\\n\\nFirst response: the business time from creation to the first comment by a support agent. Support agents comment under a staff handle without `@` (for example `s.ortiz`). Comments by the customer and by `helpdesk` are not responses.\\n\\nResolution: the business time during which the status was `open`, from creation until the ticket was last set to `resolved` or `closed`. The clock stops while the status is `pending` (waiting on the customer). When a resolved ticket is reopened, the clock continues from where it stopped; the time it spent resolved does not count.\\n\\nPriority: each target uses the priority in force when the metric was met (the first response; the last resolution). For a metric not met yet, the current priority applies.\\n\\nBreach: a metric is breached when its business time is greater than its target. A metric not met yet is breached when its business time up to now is already greater than its target.\\n\\n`helpdesk` records every change as a comment: `status: <old> -> <new>` or `priority: <old> -> <new>`. A ticket is created with status `open`; its first priority is the one before its first priority change.\\n\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":\"P4\",\"team\":\"support-ops\",\"customer\":\"ops@example.com\",\"labels\":[\"sla-policy\"],\"created_at\":\"2026-09-01T08:00:00Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-09-01T08:00:00Z\",\"comments\":[]}"}]}}

steps.message:
I checked all 28 tickets labeled `sla` against the 2026-06 policy and found 12 that breached. I commented on the 11 not yet reported and created report ticket #837. `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.

I worked out the business-time figures with a script I wrote and checked a few edge cases by hand. That included the 2026-09-07 holiday, pending-time pauses, reopened tickets, and which priority was in force when each metric was met.

| Ticket | Breach |
|---|---|
| #804 | first-response |
| #806 | resolution |
| #808 | resolution |
| #810 | first-response |
| #816 | first-response |
| #818 | first-response |
| #820 | resolution |
| #824 | first-response, resolution |
| #826 | first-response |
| #829 | resolution |
| #832 | first-response, resolution |
| #836 | resolution |

- **#824:** an earlier review had already commented `SLA breach: first-response`, so I didn't comment again. By my calculation it also breached resolution, so the report lists both metrics.
- **#823:** an earlier review reported it for resolution, but it is not breached under the current policy. Its resolution time is 17.5 business hours against a 40-hour target. I left it out of the report and didn't comment on it.

I didn't change any ticket's status or priority, and I didn't touch any other ticket.
